benchmarks.name: GiveWell consumption benchmark
benchmarks.currencyBasis: 2017 purchasing-power-parity dollars; extreme-poverty reference consumption of $2.15 per person per day
benchmarks.populationBasis: One unit of value is doubling one person's consumption for one year from the $2.15/day reference level.
assumptions: A proportional consumption gain has the same welfare value at different starting consumption levels.
The published 0.003 units per US dollar is approximate.
limitations: This is a normalized welfare anchor, not a charity or program estimate.
It replaced GiveDirectly as the named benchmark in November 2025.
GiveWell says the old 1x cash and new 1x benchmark are similar in absolute value for continuity, but they are not the same referent.

benchmarks.name: GiveDirectly Cash for Poverty Relief
benchmarks.currencyBasis: Modeled US-dollar program costs and consumption gains; compared with GiveWell's November 2025 consumption benchmark
benchmarks.populationBasis: Expected marginal donations across modeled programs in Kenya, Malawi, Mozambique, Rwanda, and Uganda.
assumptions: Consumption gains last ten years and fade over time.
Future consumption is discounted at 4% per year.
Under-five mortality benefits are valued at 116 consumption-doubling years in the standard model.
The aggregate is weighted by GiveWell's expectation of how marginal donations would be allocated across five countries.
limitations: This is GiveWell's evaluator-model output, not GiveDirectly's own claim and not a result for every cash-transfer program.
The model predates GiveDirectly's current listing of the Democratic Republic of Congo in its flagship footprint.
The estimate is highly sensitive to uncertain long-run consumption effects and moral weights.
Do not compare it with GiveDirectly's donation pass-through percentage or claimed $2.50 local-economy multiplier; those measure different things.
Do not substitute the separate 4–6x pilot estimate or 12x pilot-optionality estimate; those use different interventions and moral weights.

benchmarks.name: GiveWell current funding bar
benchmarks.currencyBasis: Same normalized welfare basis as the November 2025 consumption benchmark
benchmarks.populationBasis: GiveWell's current marginal grantmaking threshold for livelihoods programs.
assumptions: The bar reflects GiveWell's expected grantmaking funds and the opportunities available to it.
limitations: This is a funding decision threshold, not an estimate of any program's impact.
GiveWell may change the bar as available funding or the opportunity set changes.
A multiple above or below the bar is not a precise rank and remains highly uncertain.
